answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a bond that is slashed when its actions trigger independently verified fraud proofs. To avoid trusting a single judge, validators commit to a pulse of sampled decisions, then reveal a cipher-derived audit seed that selects cases for replay; matching decisions create an echo of evidence across validators. One operator can still create many accounts, but must lock capital in every one and risks losing it, so sybils become costly rather than free.
